learning_outcomes.text: Knows conventional and advanced materials applicable in Mechanical Engineering, their synthesis procedures and treatments, as well as their joining technologies and surface treatments and coatings.

Knows the processes of deterioration and damage of mechanical components in service, appropriate design criteria and certain in-service inspection techniques, and systematically analyzes, in the case of in-service failures, the mechanism and root cause of the same.
Selects materials in mechanical systems taking into account their application.

syllabus_topics: METALLIC AND NON-METALLIC MATERIALS. Ferrous alloys. Non-ferrous alloys. Special alloys: Superalloys, ODS alloys, shape memory alloys, metallic glasses, metallic foams. Non-Metallic Materials. Properties and applications.

JOINING: Welding. Structure of welds in ferrous and non-ferrous alloys. Weldability. Weld defects and their causes. Mechanical and microstructural testing of metallurgical joints. Adhesives. Mechanisms of adhesive bonding.
SURFACE ENGINEERING. Classification. Classic and advanced surface treatments and coatings. Laser applied to surfaces. Industrial applications.

IN-SERVICE FAILURE ANALYSIS. Design Life. Remaining Life. In-service inspection techniques. Methodology of damage and failure analysis in metallic materials. Practical cases. Techniques and instruments for investigating in-service failures. Fractography. Technical report. The Expert in court.
teaching_methods: Presentation of course assignments and subsequent debates
Group work monitoring tutorials, in-person or via telematic methods

assessment_methods.method: Written exam on theoretical-practical content (Global Test)
Written exam on conceptual and procedural content of practicals (Global Test)

assessment_rules: For continuous evaluation, laboratory practicals must be approved independently. A minimum grade of 4 (out of 10) is required in each of the two written theoretical-practical tests for them to be combined with group assignments. The overall final grade must be at least 5 out of 10 to pass. For the global test, students must obtain a minimum of 4 out of 10 in each part (theoretical-practical and practical content exams), and the weighted sum of grades must be at least 5 out of 10. In the second call, the same tests and conditions apply for both continuous and global evaluation students. Students who followed continuous evaluation but did not pass certain components must complete them in the global test, achieving a minimum of 4 out of 10 in those parts and an overall total of at least 5 out of 10.
